I write R in [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/), on more than one Windows machine. These pages describe the set-up in enough detail that I (or you) can rebuild it, and include my configuration files.

## My set-up in short {#in-short}

I use **VS Code with the [vscode-R](https://github.com/REditorSupport/vscode-R) extension** for all my R work, on Windows.
R runs in **[radian](https://github.com/randy3k/radian)**, a modern R console with syntax highlighting and multi-line editing, opened in a terminal panel docked on the right.
Plots go to the **[httpgd](https://github.com/nx10/httpgd)** viewer inside VS Code.
The **`languageserver`** package gives autocompletion, hover help and go to definition; **`lintr`** checks the code as I type, and **`styler`** formats it when I ask.
I write documents, slides and this website in **[Quarto](https://quarto.org/)**, with the Quarto extension for preview and code-chunk execution.
**[rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig)** manages several R versions side by side, and **[renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/)** with **[targets](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/)** keeps each project reproducible ([project template](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/Project_template)).
Git work happens in the built-in Source Control view, with **GitLens**, **Git Graph** and the **GitHub Pull Requests** extension.
For AI help I use **GitHub Copilot** and **Claude Code**.
The look is the built-in **Visual Studio Dark** theme with **vscode-icons**, and a set of [custom keybindings](keybindings.qmd) (for example `Ctrl+Shift+M` for the pipe) makes the common R actions one keystroke.
Everything is kept in one VS Code profile called `R`, synced between my machines.

It pairs with two other things I use daily:

- my [**project template**](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/Project_template) for reproducible R projects (renv, targets, tests, instructions for coding assistants);
- the [**R Version Switcher**](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/r-version-switcher) extension, for per-project R versions ([R versions](r_versions.qmd)).

## The idea

**One environment on every machine, with no machine-specific paths.**

- VS Code's [Settings Sync](profiles_sync.qmd) carries settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks and extensions between machines.
- That only works if the synced files contain no user names and no install paths. So nothing in them says *where* R is or *which* version: VS Code starts `radian`, radian starts `R`, and both are found on `PATH`.
- [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig) decides which R that is, per machine, with `rig default`. Changing the R version never touches VS Code.
- The few things Sync cannot carry ([task scripts, `.Rprofile`, PowerShell profiles](outside_vscode.qmd)) follow the same rule. `.Rprofile` and the PowerShell profiles are shared through OneDrive; the task scripts I copy by hand.

## How the pieces fit {#how-the-pieces-fit}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph sync["Settings Sync"]
    profile["VS Code profile 'R'<br/>settings · keybindings<br/>snippets · tasks · extensions"]
  end
  subgraph machine["Each machine"]
    path["PATH"]
    radian["radian<br/>(Python 3.12)"]
    rig["rig shortcuts<br/>C:\Program Files\R\bin"]
    r["R x.y.z<br/>(rig default)"]
    lib["package library<br/>per R version"]
    rprofile[".Rprofile<br/>(OneDrive)"]
  end
  profile -- "r.consolePath: radian" --> path
  path --> radian
  path --> rig
  radian -- "R on PATH" --> rig
  profile -- "language server, help" --> rig
  rig --> r
  r --> lib
  r --> rprofile
```

## Rebuild from scratch {#rebuild-from-scratch}

On a new Windows machine:

1. **Install** everything in the order on [Install, in order](install.qmd) (steps 1–9).
2. **VS Code profile.** Either sign in to Settings Sync (on my own machines), or create a profile called `R` and fill it in from the published files:
   - settings: [settings.json](settings.qmd#the-full-file) → *Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)*;
   - keybindings: [keybindings.json](keybindings.qmd#the-full-file) → *Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts (JSON)*;
   - snippets and tasks: [Snippets and tasks](snippets_tasks.qmd);
   - extensions: `install_extensions.ps1` from [Extensions](extensions.qmd#installing-them).
3. **Sync gotcha.** Make sure `settingsSync.ignoredSettings` is also in the **Default** profile ([why](profiles_sync.qmd#the-gotcha)).
4. **Outside VS Code**: put `.Rprofile` in `Documents`, the task scripts in `%USERPROFILE%\.vscode-scripts\`, and run `rig system fix-r-alias` ([details](outside_vscode.qmd)).
5. **Check `PATH`** against the [rules](outside_vscode.qmd#path-rules): no `R_HOME`, no `R-x.y.z\bin`, Python 3.12 first.
6. **Restart VS Code completely**, open an R terminal, approve the `sess` installation it asks for, and run `plot(1:10)` ([test](install.qmd#restart-vs-code-and-test)).
